text:
B: Hiya. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yes, hello. I'm Nasreen.
B: Darren. Nice to meet you.
A: You too. You are the last one for me.
B: Same here. Where are you?
A: Walsall.
B: Stourbridge. Other side of the Black Country.
A: Oh, not far.
B: No. What do you do?
A: Erm, I'm between jobs. Before, I was receptionist at a GP surgery.
B: Oh, right. You might be able to help me, actually.
A: Yes?
B: My mum's surgery. She's not been so good lately, and I'm the one sorting it all out. Getting her in is a nightmare. You ring at eight, you're forty in the queue, then there's nothing left.
A: Yes, yes, that's normal, sorry. Erm, ask them for the online system, the app, they can link you to her account, with her permission. Then you can request online, sometimes it's easier. And tell them she has a carer, that's you. If you are on the record as carer, sometimes they can help more, they ring you back. And ask for the same doctor, if she likes one. Continuity, they call it.
B: Linked account. I didn't know you could do that.
A: Yes. I do it for my auntie also. I translate for her.
B: That's handy. Thanks. I'll ask them.
A: Is she very poorly, your mum?
B: Just slowing down a bit. Forgets things. She's alright.
A: Inshallah she will be okay. My mother is the same, but she is in Pakistan. Far away.
B: That must be hard.
A: Yes. I talk to her every day, on the phone. But, you know.
B: Yeah.
A: You work with what?
B: Gas engineer. Boilers.
A: Oh. Our boiler, the house is rented, every winter it stops. The landlord sends somebody, he hits it, it works for one week.
B: Hits it?
A: Yes, with the hand. Like this.
B: That's not a repair, that. What's it doing, losing pressure?
A: I don't know. It says something, a number. F, something.
B: Fault code. Take a picture of it next time and give it to the landlord in writing. If it keeps going, he's got to get it properly sorted. You're entitled to heating.
A: Okay. Picture, then writing. Thank you.
B: No bother.
A: You have family?
B: Wife, two kids. And a spaniel, Bonnie.
A: Spaniel. The ones with the long ears?
B: That's her. Rolls in everything.
A: Ha. My son wants a dog. I said no, who will walk it?
B: That's what I said. Guess who walks it.
A: You?
B: Every morning, before work.
